claim: CoT exemplars (steps before the answer) lift large models sharply on multi-step math: PaLM 540B GSM8K 17.9 -> 56.9, Codex 19.7 -> 63.1, GPT-3 15.6 -> 46.9 (Wei 2022). Re-run in other papers at similar levels (56.5 greedy CoT in the self-consistency paper).
agent_test: Compare direct answer vs brief stepwise answer on our multi-step items at equal total tokens.

claim: A bare trigger 'Let's think step by step' gives much of the gain with no exemplars: text-davinci-002 MultiArith 17.7 -> 78.7, GSM8K 10.4 -> 40.7; PaLM 540B GSM8K 12.5 -> 43.0 (Kojima 2022).
agent_test: Zero-shot trigger vs no trigger vs hand-written scaffold step, equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The benefit depended on model scale: in 2022-era models CoT hurt or did nothing below roughly 100B parameters (LaMDA 420M GSM8K 2.6 -> 0.4; 137B 6.5 -> 14.3). Modern strong models are past this threshold, so it is mostly historical for our agent.
agent_test: Not needed for a strong backbone; only check if we ever use a small model for sub-calls.

claim: Gain grows with problem difficulty and number of steps; on one-step or easy problems gain is zero or negative (Wei SingleOp, Kojima SingleEq/AddSub, CommonsenseQA drop 68.8 -> 64.6).
agent_test: Route easy items to a direct answer; test whether a cheap difficulty gate saves tokens without accuracy loss.

claim: Ablations: equation-only, filler dots of equal length, and reasoning placed after the answer do not reproduce the GSM8K gain in 2022 models; natural-language steps before the answer matter.
agent_test: Check on our agent that thinking comes before commit; a 'think after answering' arm should give no gain.

claim: Filler tokens give no gain in ordinary pretrained models (Lanham: no gain at any length), though trained toy transformers can use dots for parallel tasks with dense supervision. Extra compute alone is not the mechanism for prompted models.
agent_test: Equal-token control: filler vs real reasoning vs none.

claim: Self-consistency (sample many chains, majority vote) adds large gains over greedy CoT: PaLM GSM8K 56.5 -> 74.4 (+17.9), SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2, StrategyQA +6.4, ARC-c +3.9. But it costs about 40x tokens, and on Blocksworld it dropped performance.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: one long chain vs k short chains with vote.

claim: Agreement among sampled chains is a usable confidence signal (strong correlation with accuracy on GSM8K). Gap search: confidence-weighted voting (CISC, 9 models, 4 datasets) cuts samples by over 40% on average, and adaptive stopping (17 datasets) cuts budget up to 7.9x at under 0.1% accuracy loss. Within-question discrimination matters more than global calibration.
agent_test: Use vote share as a trigger for extra checking; measure calibration on our items.

claim: Exemplar correctness is not the main driver: invalid-reasoning exemplars keep 80-90% of CoT performance (GSM8K 39.5 vs 48.5, standard 15.4); relevance to the query and step order matter (no relevance 11.0, no coherence 23.1). Chain style also robust to annotator (Wei). Gap search: in long-CoT fine-tuning, wrong-answer samples cost only 3.2 points while shuffled steps cost 13.3 on AIME24 (training, not prompting; not a test on prompted invalid exemplars with current models).
agent_test: Scramble or corrupt scaffold examples and see if the agent degrades; if not, content of examples is not the lever.

claim: The text of a CoT may matter more than its symbols: replacing numbers or making equations invalid barely changes solve rate, while removing text hurts (Madaan 2022). Caveat: single group, 2022 models.
agent_test: Ablate wording vs equation content in our scratch notes.

claim: Prompt wording is fragile: MultiArith with different trigger phrases ranged 18.8 to 78.7; misleading triggers collapse.
agent_test: Fix one trigger and test two or three paraphrases to see variance before claiming any gain.

claim: Complexity-based selection and decomposition help: more-step exemplars (+5.3 avg, up to +18) and least-to-most (SCAN at least 99% vs 16% CoT, code-davinci-002).
agent_test: Test decomposition operator vs plain CoT on length-generalisation items.

claim: A CoT is often not a faithful account of why the answer was given. Biasing features change answers while chains never mention the bias (Turpin: GPT-3.5 -36.3 points under suggested answer); Claude 3.7 and R1 verbalise used hints only 25% and 39% of the time (Chen 2025); implicit post-hoc rationalisation seen without hints (up to 13% in production models). Gap search: reasoning models do better but still miss cues: R1 names the professor cue 59% (non-reasoning best 13%), other cue types near 0% for all (Chua and Evans).
agent_test: Inject a misleading hint into the task and check whether the agent's trace cites it; never treat the trace as evidence of the cause.

claim: Faithfulness varies by task and fell with model size in the 2023 test: early-answering changes the answer >60% on AQuA but <10% on ARC/OpenBookQA; 13B model more faithful than 175B on 7 of 8 tasks.
agent_test: Early-truncation test: cut our agent's chain and see how often the answer changes, per task type.

claim: Harder questions and longer chains are less faithful: unfaithful CoT averaged 2064 tokens vs 1439 faithful (Claude 3.7); GPQA 44% (relative) less faithful than MMLU. Outcome RL raises faithfulness then plateaus (28% MMLU, 20% GPQA).
agent_test: Check whether longer traces on our agent correlate with lower self-report accuracy.

claim: Across 100+ papers, CoT helps mainly on math, symbolic and logic tasks (mean +12.3, +14.2, +6.9) and little elsewhere (56.8 vs 56.1). On MMLU up to 95% of gain comes from questions with an equals sign.
agent_test: Gate thinking by task type: symbolic or numeric steps get chains, knowledge recall does not; compare tokens and accuracy. (Consistent with Wei and Kojima easy/commonsense null results, but those are older and narrower.)

claim: Much of the CoT gain is executing symbolic steps; a plan handed to a tool or solver beats the model executing it in text.
agent_test: Plan then external execution (code, solver) vs written-out execution at equal tokens.

claim: For modern non-reasoning chat models, a CoT prompt gives small average gains but more variability and lower perfect-answer rate; for models that already reason, an explicit CoT request adds about nothing and costs 20-80% more time (Meincke 2025, GPQA Diamond, 25 trials each: Gemini Flash 2.0 +0.135 avg but -0.131 at 25/25). Gap search: CoT also lowers instruction-following in 13 of 14 models on IFEval (Llama3-8B 75.2 -> 59.0, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 86.5 -> 79.5) and all on ComplexBench; longer reasoning lowers accuracy on distractor tasks (Claude Opus 4 near 100% -> 85-90%).
agent_test: Do not tell a reasoning backbone to think step by step; measure answer variance, not just mean.

claim: CoT can hurt: tasks where verbal deliberation hurts humans also hurt models (GPT-4o artificial grammar 87.5 -> 64.4; face recognition 64.0 -> 51.2; exception learning 331% more rounds), but not all models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet unchanged in grammar). CoT helped on one NLI inconsistency task. Gap search: harm is reproducible on Claude models in other task types (instruction following, distractor counting), though not on grammar.
agent_test: Include intuition-type perceptual or statistical-learning items in our test set where thinking may hurt.

claim: Under a wrong suggestion, zero-shot CoT can pull a model off right answers (GPT-3.5 39.5 -> 23.3), while few-shot CoT reduces this sensitivity; irrelevant clauses cut accuracy sharply (GSM-NoOp drops up to 65%).
agent_test: Distractor and misleading-hint items: check that the agent's chain does not follow them.

claim: CoT transfers poorly beyond the prompt's problem class: on Blocksworld GPT-4 reached 59.3% only with a stacking-specific prompt (zero-shot 3.8%, general n-shot 6-16%, universal-algorithm CoT 37-51%), and gains vanish as stack size grows.
agent_test: Generalisation test: length or size beyond any worked example; do not expect chains to extend.

claim: More thinking is not monotonic: accuracy is an inverted U with CoT length, and o1-like models overthink easy items (1,953% more tokens for 2+3; first solution round usually holds the right answer). Gap search: within one question, shortest sampled chains beat the longest by up to 34.5 points (4 reasoning models); R1 uses at least 5x the tokens of Claude 3.7 Sonnet for equal AIME 25 accuracy.
agent_test: Sweep a token cap per difficulty tier and find the knee; set the budget there.

claim: The 'illusion of thinking' collapse at high puzzle complexity is partly a grading and output-limit artifact (Opus and Lawsen: Hanoi move lists exceed limits; some River Crossing instances impossible). Claim of reasoning collapse is contested. Gap search: Hanoi N=15 as a Lua program done in under 5,000 tokens by four frontier models (preliminary, no trial counts); River Crossing N>=6 with capacity 3 is unsolvable. Larger-budget reruns not found.
agent_test: Use a generating-program output instead of full move lists when testing long-horizon items.

claim: Chains exist latently: branching at the first decoding token and ranking by answer confidence recovers CoT without prompts (PaLM-2 L GSM8K 34.8 -> 63.2; Mistral-7B 9.9 -> 25.1).
agent_test: Not directly usable with an API-only backbone; note only.

claim: Theory: transformers without intermediate tokens sit near TC0; log-length chains add little, linear-length chains add regular languages, polynomial chains reach P (Merrill and Sabharwal; Feng et al. agree). Longer chains buy real expressive power for serial problems.
agent_test: Choose tasks needing serial depth to test whether more steps help; parallel tasks should not benefit.

claim: Zero-shot CoT raises harmful or stereotyped outputs in sensitive prompts (text-davinci-003 refusal 78% direct vs 25% zero-shot CoT, one example).
agent_test: Run a refusal or bias check with and without the thinking step.

claim: Scratchpads were the precursor: emitting intermediate state lets models do long addition and program tracing (polynomial eval 8.8 -> 20.1 few-shot), but with only 374 MBPP tasks scratchpad did worse than direct (5 vs 10 percent).
agent_test: Background only.

claim: For reasoning models, short chains beat long chains within the same question and a short-m@k vote (stop at first m finished chains) matches or beats majority vote at up to 40% fewer thinking tokens (Hassid 2025: 4 models, AIME24/25, HMMT, GPQA-D, 20 samples each; shortest vs longest up to +34.5 points).
agent_test: On our items, sample k chains, keep the shortest m, vote; compare with majority at equal total tokens.

claim: The best test-time compute depends on difficulty: compute-optimal allocation by difficulty bin gives the same accuracy as best-of-N at up to 4x less compute; extra search hurts on easy bins and does little on the hardest (Snell 2024, MATH, PaLM 2). A cheap difficulty estimate captures part of this.
agent_test: Add a cheap difficulty gate (e.g. first-pass vote agreement) that picks no-think, brief think, or sample-and-verify.

claim: Inverse scaling is reproducible in current models from several vendors: with distractors or spurious features longer reasoning lowers accuracy (Claude Opus 4 near 100% -> 85-90%; DeepSeek R1 70% -> 30% with five distractors), and irrelevant trailing text raises error rates of reasoning models by over 300% in adversarial search (CatAttack).
agent_test: Test whether a one-line ignore-irrelevant-information instruction and a short reasoning budget help on perturbed items at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit CoT lowers instruction-following accuracy (13 of 14 models on IFEval, all on ComplexBench; e.g. Llama3-8B 75.2 -> 59.0, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 86.5 -> 79.5); a per-item gate (classifier-selective reasoning) recovers most of the loss.
agent_test: Gate thinking by item type: no step-by-step on format-constrained or simple-constraint tasks.

claim: Handing arithmetic to an interpreter is robust where written-out CoT is not: Codex GSM-Hard CoT 65.6 -> 20.1 vs PAL 72.0 -> 61.5; GSM8K majority@40 PAL 80.4 vs Minerva 78.5 (Gao 2023). Not token-matched, and 2022-era models.
agent_test: Equal-token test of tool execution vs written-out execution on a current model (gap 5 still open).

claim: CoT gains on clean benchmarks overstate performance on perturbed items: GPT-3.5 CoT GSM8K 74.17 -> GSM-Plus 62.92, critical-thinking subset 40.83 (Li 2024); sub-goal prompting plus voting recovers some points.
agent_test: Include unanswerable and contradictory items; require the agent to say cannot be answered when so.
